primary_falsifiable_hypothesis.name: rule-first serialization routing for length-overflow tasks
primary_falsifiable_hypothesis.statement: If candidate generation is routed to compact rule/program hypotheses without materializing full predicted grids for tasks whose candidate stage would exceed the fixed output budget, then 0607ce86 and 06df4c85 should become parseable under the same model/budget, and at least one should gain exact candidate-oracle coverage when rules are executed deterministically.
primary_falsifiable_hypothesis.frozen_comparator: ARC-R020 compact-hypothesis candidate generation on the same task IDs and model settings
primary_falsifiable_hypothesis.success_threshold: 2/2 candidate stages parseable and >=1/2 mechanically verified candidate coverage, with no full-grid candidate serialization
primary_falsifiable_hypothesis.falsification: Either task still fails to produce a parseable compact rule within the same token budget, or both are parseable but deterministic execution yields 0/2 exact candidate coverage.

secondary_routing_hypothesis.statement: Route by morphology rather than universal object prompting: retain direct/local mapping for 0d3d703e; use relation-specific primitives for 05f2a901 and 070dd51e; use attribute-binding primitives for 00dbd492.
secondary_routing_hypothesis.testable_requirement: A future matched routing experiment must mechanically derive comparator coverage and predeclare per-family task IDs before calls.

adversarial_alternatives: finish_reason=length may reflect verbose model behavior rather than intrinsic task morphology; compact prompting alone could fix parseability without a new representation.
The two overflow tasks are too small a sample to justify a general router; the hypothesis is deliberately local until replicated.
Parseable zero-coverage tasks may fail because three candidates are too few rather than because the inferred primitive family is wrong.
Candidate rules can sound morphologically appropriate while still being semantically wrong; taxonomy labels are diagnostics, not proof of the true ARC rule.
Hosted deterministic inference can vary between runs, so any future treatment requires a matched comparator and mechanical coverage accounting.
next_recommendation: Test compact rule-first candidate serialization on the two repeated length-overflow tasks before spending inference on another universal representation prompt.
